item.title: Indonesia Sole Candidate for UN Human Rights Council President
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia recently announced that Asia-Pacific countries had picked Jakarta as their sole candidate for the 2026 UN Human Rights Council presidency. The council’s presidency rotates among its members every year, representing a different region each time. It will be Asia-Pacific’s turn to lead the council next year, and this regional group has nominated Indonesia to assume the 2026 leadership. item.description: Jakarta. Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) opened stronger Wednesday morning at 8,597 added 13 points or 0.15% in the range of 8,591 – 8,611. item.title: BNI Provides Trauma Healing for Children Affected by Floods in Southeast Aceh
item.description: Southeast Aceh. State lender PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, or BNI, is assisting in the psychosocial recovery of children affected by flash floods in Leuser Village, Southeast Aceh Regency. This effort underscores BNI's commitment to post-disaster recovery that focuses not only on physical and logistical assistance, but also on mental recovery and psychological well-being of vulnerable groups, especially children. item.title: Indonesia Targets 15.6 Billion Liters of Biodiesel to Save $8B in Diesel Imports
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia plans to distribute 15.6 billion liters of biodiesel in 2026, a move expected to reduce fossil diesel imports by Rp 139 trillion ($8.3 billion), according to the Energy and Mineral Resources Ministry. The government is currently implementing the mandatory B40 program, which requires diesel fuel supplied under government schemes to contain a 40% biofuel blend, up from a 35% blend last year. item.title: Back-to-Back Records: Antam Gold Reaches New Peak at Rp 2.59 Million
item.description: Jakarta. Gold prices at state-owned miner Aneka Tambang surged to a new record on Wednesday, with Antam bullion jumping Rp 29,000 to Rp 2,590,000 ($154.53) per gram as the rally showed no signs of cooling. Data from the Logam Mulia website showed Antam gold had already set a previous all-time high a day earlier, after prices spiked Rp 59,000 to Rp 2,561,000 per gram on Tuesday. item.title: Jakarta Launches Rp2.62 Trillion Flood Control Project
item.description: Jakarta. The Jakarta provincial government has officially launched a large-scale flood control initiative worth Rp2.62 trillion ($156.25 million), aiming to strengthen the capital’s resilience against chronic flooding and coastal inundation. The program, dubbed JakTirta, focuses on reinforcing embankments in northern Jakarta, expanding water retention capacity, and upgrading pumping systems that form the backbone of the city’s flood mitigation efforts. item.title: Indonesia Expects 1.45 Million Foreign Tourists on Year-End Holidays
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia estimates that it will record 1.45 million foreign tourist arrivals during the year-end holidays, according to Tourism Minister Widiyanti Putri Wardhana. The minister did not go into details on where these foreign tourists would primarily come from. However, Indonesia is a popular tourist spot for Malaysians, Australians, and Chinese nationals, the Central Statistics Agency (BPS) data showed. item.title: Whoosh Passenger Numbers Surge Ahead of Christmas
item.description: Jakarta. Passenger traffic at the Whoosh high-speed rail station in Halim, East Jakarta, surged on Wednesday, a day ahead of Christmas 2025, with more than 23,000 people expected to travel, up over 20 percent from normal daily volumes. Thousands of people crowded Halim Station from early morning as residents of Greater Jakarta flocked to the high-speed railway service for trips to Bandung and other parts of West Java. item.title: Govt Offers $119 Million Export Financing to Support Furniture Exports
item.description: Jakarta.
